newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: About 50,000 demonstrators mass in Belgrade square.
newsitem.headline: About 50,000 demonstrators mass in Belgrade square.

text.p: About 50,000 demonstrators massed in a Belgrade square on Sunday in the 42nd straight day of demonstrations in a crisis over local election results.

Serbian security police, enforcing a ban on street marches after a December 24 riot caused by protesters and government loyalists, lined roads as opposition leaders addressed the crowd, eyewitnesses said.

There have been daily street protests in Belgrade since the ruling Socialist Party (SPS) annulled November 17 municipal elections won by the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition. Some demonstrations drew up to a quarter of a million people.

Zajedno, backed later by findings of a mission from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), accused the SPS of rampant vote rigging and wants its victories reinstated in 14 cities including Belgrade.
Western governments have warned Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic he will get no financial aid unless he concedes SPS electoral defeats and undertakes democratic reforms.
In a statement issued before Sunday's rally, Zajedno accused Milosevic of resorting to a state of emergency and police terror in a bid to snuff out opposition protests.

"Large police forces have been deployed in all towns in Serbia to prevent citizens from expressing their grievances by walking around," said the statement, quoted by the independent Belgrade news agency Beta.

It said citizens would continue protest marches until they won "recognition of their fundamental rights" and would mark the New Year holiday, Orthodox Christmas and the Serbian New Year (mid-January) in the streets.
Milosevic, a communist-style strongman determined to keep 50 years of unbroken rule by his party intact, was expected to respond to the OSCE report in the coming week.
